Appendix D. Flow Storyboards

Every step of every flow of Section 7 (26 flows, 121 steps), as the prototype shows it with the step bar at the bottom. Read each flow left to right, top to bottom; the text under each picture is the step bar's explanation.

D.1 FL-00 Tour the deputy dean task queue

Deputy dean · 2 steps

Step 1 of 2. Hakim lands on the task queue: everything waiting for a decision, oldest flagged as overdue. (#/dd/queue)
Step 2 of 2. Tabs filter by area and the counts follow. Click a row to open its decision screen. (#/dd/queue?area=results)

D.2 FL-01 Sign in with SSO and MFA, land on the task page

Any staff · 3 steps

Step 1 of 3. Staff sign in with their UTeM Microsoft account. There is no separate MCMS password. Click Continue. (#/signin)
Step 2 of 3. Roles that decide on records need a second step. Enter any 6-digit code and verify. (#/signin/mfa)
Step 3 of 3. Hakim lands on what needs him today: the task queue, not an empty home page. (#/dd/queue)

D.3 FL-02 Propose a UMC, fix the SLT, submit

Lecturer · 5 steps

Step 1 of 5. Dr. Aina starts a new proposal. Pick "Modules from a UTeM credit course" and a parent course to see the category and the reason. A 30 h own offering would be an MCE only. (#/lec/new)
Step 2 of 5. Her Software Testing draft has modules of 40 + 38 + 32 = 110 h. The checks panel shows the blocking error and Submit is disabled with the reason beside it. (#/lec/proposal/ST?tab=mods)
Step 3 of 5. Click "Set module 3 to 42 h" (or type 42). The total becomes 120 h, the error clears, and the panel shows one warning about an outcome with no assessment. (#/lec/proposal/ST?tab=mods)
Step 4 of 5. Click Submit for review, write a short response to the warning, and confirm. The status becomes Submitted and the content locks. (#/lec/proposal/ST?tab=mods)
Step 5 of 5. Hakim Rahman now has a task "Assign reviewers" for Software Testing. (#/dd/queue?area=proposals)

D.4 FL-03 Review a colleague's proposal

Lecturer as reviewer · 4 steps

Step 1 of 4. Dr. Aina has an invitation to review Cyber Security Operations Fundamentals, due 30 Oct. (#/lec/reviews)
Step 2 of 4. Step 1: declare a conflict of interest. The proposal stays closed until you do. Choose "I have no conflict of interest" and confirm. Choosing a conflict declines the review instead. (#/lec/review/RV-031)
Step 3 of 4. Step 2: rate each item Satisfactory or Needs amendment. A Needs amendment rating needs a comment and can be marked blocking. (#/lec/review/RV-031)
Step 4 of 4. Step 3: choose Support, Amend or Do not support, add a summary, and submit. Submit stays disabled until everything is filled. (#/lec/review/RV-031)

D.5 FL-04 Endorse a proposal, then record the Senate decision

Deputy dean · 7 steps

Step 1 of 7. Two proposal tasks: endorse Database Systems, and record Senate's decision on Applied Data Analytics. (#/dd/queue?area=proposals)
Step 2 of 7. Endorse is blocked. Open Comments: the answered blocking comment shows the lecturer's response, so read it and click Mark resolved with a reason. The other blocking comment has no response yet and cannot be resolved. (#/dd/proposal/DB)
Step 3 of 7. Dr. Aina responds to the open blocking comment. It becomes answered. (#/lec/proposal/DB?tab=comments)
Step 4 of 7. Back with the deputy dean: resolve the answered comment, verify the category on the Review summary tab, then click Endorse and confirm. A task to record the Senate decision is created. (#/dd/proposal/DB)
Step 5 of 7. The decision pack for Senate 8/2026 now shows the endorsement. Print pack opens the A4 document. (#/dd/pack?id=DB)
Step 6 of 7. Senate met on 14 Oct. Enter the meeting date and the wording from the minutes, choose Approved, and confirm. The dialog says no QV or credit status is set. (#/dd/senate/ADA)
Step 7 of 7. Both proposals now show their new status. Approval is one decision; QV and credit are separate. (#/dd/proposals)

D.6 FL-05 Create an offering and confirm readiness

Lecturer, deputy dean · 4 steps

Step 1 of 4. Dr. Aina creates a new cohort for the approved Data Structures version. (#/lec/offering/new)
Step 2 of 4. She uploads the one open item (facilitator qualification evidence) and sends the checklist to the deputy dean. (#/lec/readiness/DS-2027-1)
Step 3 of 4. Hakim can only confirm once the checklist is sent. Click Accept evidence on the new item, choose Ready, and record the decision. Ready with conditions and Not ready are the other choices. (#/dd/readiness/DS-2027-1)
Step 4 of 4. The cohort is now Open and appears in the public catalogue. (#/public/catalogue)

D.7 FL-06 Find, register and pay

Student · 6 steps

Step 1 of 6. Amir reads the public offering page. Credit is not claimed because QV ends before the cohort does. Click Register. (#/public/offering/CND-2027-1)
Step 2 of 6. Step 1: eligibility checks pass and he confirms his phone number. Click Continue. (#/st/register/CND-2027-1?step=1)
Step 3 of 6. Step 2: tick both the recognition statement and the PDPA notice. The statement says credit depends on QV renewal. Click Continue to payment. (#/st/register/CND-2027-1?step=2)
Step 4 of 6. Step 3: pay with the dummy card, then confirm Pay now in the dialog. Any card number except 4000 0000 0000 0002 succeeds. (#/st/register/CND-2027-1?step=3)
Step 5 of 6. Step 4: confirmation with the enrolment ID and how to open UCreds. The registration now shows under Registrations and payments. (#/st/register/CND-2027-1?step=4)
Step 6 of 6. The new registration is listed as Enrolled with its receipt link. (#/st/enrolments)

D.8 FL-06b Payment failure and retry

Student · 3 steps

Step 1 of 3. Amir pays for Lean Six Sigma Yellow Belt. Replace the card number with 4000 0000 0000 0002 and click Pay, then confirm. (#/st/register/LSS-2026-12?step=3)
Step 2 of 3. The failure shows inside the payment block with a reference. The registration stays Pending payment and nothing was charged. Put back 4242 4242 4242 4242 and click Retry payment. (#/st/register/LSS-2026-12?step=3)
Step 3 of 3. After a successful retry the registration is Enrolled, with one payment only. (#/st/enrolments)

D.9 FL-07 Import UCreds results with a bad row

CODL, lecturer, deputy dean · 3 steps

Step 1 of 3. Farid chooses results-CND-2026-2.csv and clicks Check file. The report shows 22 rows ready, 2 rejected (empty marks) and a notice that this file was already imported. Click Stage 22 rows and watch the job run. Dr. Aina is told which marks are missing. Nothing becomes an achievement yet. (#/codl/ucreds)
Step 2 of 3. Now as Dr. Aina: she enters Daniel Ong's project mark and Wong Kar Seng's module 2 mark, and submits the results for verification. (#/lec/cohort/CND-2026-2)
Step 3 of 3. Now as Hakim, the deputy dean: the cohort waits for verification. Only the deputy dean can verify; CODL has no verify button. (#/dd/results)

D.10 FL-08 Verify results, then confirm completion

Deputy dean · 3 steps

Step 1 of 3. Review the 28 provisional results, then click Verify 28 results. This creates module badges only; nothing is issued yet. (#/dd/verify/DS-2026-2)
Step 2 of 3. A new task appeared for completion. Check the pre-issue checks (one learner is below the pass mark and is not issued), then Confirm completion and watch the job run. (#/dd/completion/DS-2026-2)
Step 3 of 3. Learners find issued credentials in their wallet. This is Amir's own list, showing what a participant sees. (#/st/credentials)

D.11 FL-09 Share a credential and have it verified

Student, public · 4 steps

Step 1 of 4. Amir copies the share link for his Data Structures credential and sees what an employer will see. (#/st/credential/MCMS-C-2026-000098)
Step 2 of 4. An employer opens the link: minimum fields only, status Valid. (#/public/verify/3HXP-92LD)
Step 3 of 4. A revoked credential says Revoked and shows no result. (#/public/verify/R7KD-1MQA)
Step 4 of 4. A code that does not exist says it was not found and tells the employer what to check. (#/public/verify/ZZZZ-0000)

D.12 FL-10 Correct a credential name

Deputy dean · 2 steps

Step 1 of 2. Lee Jia Hui asked for her name to be corrected. Click Start correction, check the name, give a reason and confirm. (#/dd/cred/MCMS-C-2026-000418)
Step 2 of 2. The same public link now shows the credential as Corrected, with the corrected name. (#/public/verify/7Q2M-K4PA)

D.13 FL-11 Consent to ABC deposit, confirm ACR, record deposit, see ledger

Student, deputy dean · 4 steps

Step 1 of 4. Amir opens his Cloud Native Development ACR and gives consent to deposit it in ABC. Click Give consent, then Next step. (#/st/acr/MCMS-A-2026-000214)
Step 2 of 4. Hakim sees the consented, confirmed ACR in the deposit queue. Only ACR with consent appear here. Open the row. (#/dd/acr?tab=queue)
Step 3 of 4. Open the export for ABC, go back, then enter the ABC reference and date and click Record deposit. The credit becomes Available for 10 years and Amir is told it is storage, not a transfer. (#/dd/deposit/MCMS-A-2026-000214)
Step 4 of 4. Amir sees the credit as Available with its expiry date and the ABC reference. (#/st/ledger)

D.14 FL-12 Apply for credit transfer; decide by outcome; provisionally redeemed; second use blocked

Student, deputy dean · 5 steps

Step 1 of 5. Amir's application TR-2026-0012 is under evaluation. It was submitted from the new application page; nothing more to do here. (#/st/transfer/TR-2026-0012)
Step 2 of 5. Hakim compares each outcome (all Full) and checks the ACR is deposited, valid and unused. Choose Approve, then Record decision. (#/dd/transfer/TR-2026-0012)
Step 3 of 5. The credit now shows Provisionally redeemed. It cannot be used for another application. (#/st/ledger)
Step 4 of 5. Amir starts another application. The Data Structures credit is no longer selectable and the page says why. (#/st/transfer/new)
Step 5 of 5. Wong Kar Seng's case has one outcome with no match. Approve is disabled for that line; you can only refuse it or ask for more evidence. A line whose outcomes are not rated is blocked the same way. (#/dd/transfer/TR-2026-0009)

D.15 FL-13 Stackable plan: 25% "Not yet suitable" and a suitable plan

Deputy dean · 4 steps

Step 1 of 4. Hakim opens the individual plans. Wong Kar Seng is Not yet suitable; Amir is Suitable. (#/dd/stack?tab=plans)
Step 2 of 4. Wong proposes 90 of 120 credits from outside UTeM, so only 25% is earned at UTeM. The 30% minimum fails and the suitable options are off. Note that 30% does not mean 70% transfers. (#/dd/plan/SP-2026-004)
Step 3 of 4. Amir has 95.8% at UTeM, residency met and admission recorded, so Suitable to proceed is available. Record the decision. (#/dd/plan/SP-2026-003)
Step 4 of 4. The pathway mapping behind the plans. Try adding Leadership Essentials: an MCE is refused. Then submit for Senate approval. (#/dd/pathway/PW-BITZ-1)

D.16 FL-14 QV evidence, gate, record QV result; expiry removes claims

Lecturer, deputy dean · 4 steps

Step 1 of 4. Dr. Aina keeps the QV evidence for Cloud Native Development. QV expires on 6 Dec 2026, 41 days away. (#/lec/qv/CND)
Step 2 of 4. Hakim builds the package, records the submission date and reference, then records the result. Try a validity longer than 3 years: it is refused. (#/dd/qv/CND)
Step 3 of 4. Cyber Security Operations has no completed cohort, so it cannot be Ready to submit. The button is off and says why. (#/dd/qv/CSO)
Step 4 of 4. The QV list shows alerts at 180, 90 and 30 days, and the lapse rule: when QV ends, the QV claim goes but earned credentials stay. (#/dd/quality)

D.17 FL-15 Quality review: close an action only after the effectiveness check

Lecturer, deputy dean · 4 steps

Step 1 of 4. Indicators against targets: outcome attainment is 73% against 75%. Action A3 is Done, but "Close action" is disabled until an effectiveness check exists. (#/lec/cqi/CQI-DS-2026-1)
Step 2 of 4. Click "Record effectiveness check" on A3, choose a result and add evidence. Then "Close action" becomes available. A2 changes an outcome, so it offers "Create change request". (#/lec/cqi/CQI-DS-2026-1)
Step 3 of 4. Click Submit to deputy dean and confirm. The record becomes Submitted and a task is pushed. (#/lec/cqi/CQI-DS-2026-1)
Step 4 of 4. The deputy dean sees the submitted record and confirms it. (#/dd/cqi/CQI-DS-2026-1)

D.18 FL-16 Suspend an offering with a transition plan

Deputy dean · 4 steps

Step 1 of 4. Hakim sees the periodic reviews that are due. Cloud Native Development is due on 6 Nov. (#/dd/quality?tab=periodic)
Step 2 of 4. Choose the outcome "Consider suspension or termination" and record it. That takes you to the suspension screen. (#/dd/review/CND)
Step 3 of 4. The active participants are listed. A transition plan is required. Review the notice, then confirm with a reason. Earned credentials stay valid. (#/dd/suspend/CND)
Step 4 of 4. The micro-credential now shows Suspended. (#/dd/quality?tab=susp)

D.19 FL-17 Assign a scoped role and change a setting

CODL administrator · 4 steps

Step 1 of 4. Farid searches the user list and opens a person. (#/codl/users)
Step 2 of 4. Click Assign role. Choose Reviewer, scope Specific micro-credentials (LE, which Dr. Aina does not own), a reason and an effective date. The new row appears in the table. (#/codl/user/S01842)
Step 3 of 4. Find alerts.qv_expiry_days and click Change. Enter a new value, an effective date and a reason. Then click History on the same row to see old and new values. (#/codl/settings)
Step 4 of 4. Both changes are in the audit trail with who, when and why. Click Check integrity to verify the hash chain. (#/codl/audit)

D.20 FL-18 Trace a participant from approval to credit use; audit trail

Deputy dean · 3 steps

Step 1 of 3. Hakim searches for a participant or a credential number. (#/dd/trace)
Step 2 of 3. The chain runs from approval, offering, enrolment, results, completion and credential to ACR, consent, deposit, transfer and redemption. Each step shows who acted and when. (#/dd/trace/amir)
Step 3 of 3. Wong Kar Seng's chain shows a transfer still under evaluation. Scroll to the audit table at the bottom: every action on these records is listed with who did it and when. (#/dd/trace/wong)

D.21 FL-19 End-to-end: Amir from catalogue to credit used in a degree

All roles · 17 steps

Step 1 of 17. Amir, a working engineer, finds UTeM micro-credentials on the public site. (#/public/home)
Step 2 of 17. The offering says what he will get and that completion, ACR, ABC deposit and transfer are separate decisions. (#/public/offering/CND-2027-1)
Step 3 of 17. He signs in with his UTeM learner account, accepts the recognition statement and PDPA notice, and pays (dummy service). (#/st/register/CND-2027-1)
Step 4 of 17. He studies on UCreds. MCMS shows his module progress across months. (#/st/home)
Step 5 of 17. CODL imports results from UCreds. Bad rows are rejected; good rows stay Provisional. (#/codl/ucreds)
Step 6 of 17. Dr. Aina fills the two missing marks and sends the cohort for verification. (#/lec/cohort/CND-2026-2)
Step 7 of 17. Hakim verifies results. This creates module badges only, nothing else. (Shown on Data Structures 2026/2; Amir's own cohorts were verified the same way.) (#/dd/verify/DS-2026-2)
Step 8 of 17. Hakim confirms completion as a separate step. The system checks each learner and issues Amir's Leadership Essentials certificate. It is an MCE, so no ACR follows. (#/dd/completion/LE-2026-10)
Step 9 of 17. Amir sees his credentials, including the new Leadership Essentials certificate. He opens one and copies a share link. (#/st/credentials)
Step 10 of 17. An employer opens the link without signing in and sees only name, credential, issuer, date and status. (#/public/verify/3HXP-92LD)
Step 11 of 17. Amir gives consent to deposit his ACR in the Academic Bank of Credit. (#/st/acr/MCMS-A-2026-000214)
Step 12 of 17. Hakim sees the consented ACR in the deposit queue and records the ABC reference. (#/dd/deposit/MCMS-A-2026-000214)
Step 13 of 17. Amir's ledger shows the credit Available for 10 years. It is storage, not a transfer. (#/st/ledger)
Step 14 of 17. Admitted to the degree (a separate decision), Amir can now apply with Cloud Native Development. Data Structures is already in his earlier application TR-2026-0012, and MCE credit is never selectable. (#/st/transfer/new)
Step 15 of 17. Hakim, deputy dean of the degree's faculty, decides Amir's earlier application on learning outcomes and approves. The credit becomes Provisionally redeemed. (#/dd/transfer/TR-2026-0012)
Step 16 of 17. The stackable plan checks that at least 30% of credit is still earned at UTeM, and residency. (#/dd/plan/SP-2026-003)
Step 17 of 17. Anyone authorised can trace every record from approval to credit use, with who and when. (#/dd/trace/amir)

D.22 FL-20 Industry expert comments on a proposal

Industry expert · 3 steps

Step 1 of 3. Ir. Siti Aminah Yusof has an invitation to Applied Data Analytics with Python. (#/ext/home)
Step 2 of 3. The proposal is already endorsed and waits for the Senate; comments are still accepted until that decision is recorded. Declare no conflict, then write comments. There is no rating and no recommendation for this role. Send comments and confirm. (#/ext/review/RV-033)
Step 3 of 3. The comments reach the proposer on the Comments tab, where she can respond. (#/lec/proposal/ADA?tab=comments)

D.23 FL-21 Withdraw from an enrolment

Student · 3 steps

D.24 FL-22 A visitor explores the public site

Public visitor · 5 steps

Step 1 of 5. A visitor lands on the portal. The three categories and open offerings are explained before anything else. Click Next step. (#/public/home)
Step 2 of 5. The search from the home page opens the catalogue filtered to "cloud". Use the filters on the left to narrow further. (#/public/catalogue?q=cloud)
Step 3 of 5. The offering shows modules, assessment and the credential received. Note "Credit after QV renewal" and the separate-stages notice. (#/public/offering/CND-2027-1)

Step 5 of 5. Pathways show only approved micro-credentials, with the rules and the no-automatic-degree wording. (#/public/pathways)

D.25 FL-23 An employer verifies a credential

Tan Mei Ling, HR manager (public) · 7 steps

Step 1 of 7. Tan has a candidate's credential and opens the verification page. No sign-in is needed. (#/public/verify)
Step 2 of 7. The credential is valid. Only name, credential, issuer, date and status are shown. (#/public/verify/3HXP-92LD)
Step 3 of 7. A credential that was corrected (once the deputy dean corrects it) stays valid and shows the correction date. (#/public/verify/7Q2M-K4PA)
Step 4 of 7. Before you continue, replace credential 7Q2M-K4PA here as the deputy dean (use the replace action and confirm). Then click Next step. (#/dd/cred/MCMS-C-2026-000418)
Step 5 of 7. Once replaced, the old code shows "Replaced" and links to the new credential. Employers should verify the new code instead. If you did not replace it, the page still shows the earlier result. (#/public/verify/7Q2M-K4PA)
Step 6 of 7. A revoked credential shows the revocation date and must not be relied on. (#/public/verify/R7KD-1MQA)
Step 7 of 7. An unknown code gives a neutral not-found message, not an accusation. (#/public/verify/ZZZZ-0000)

D.26 FL-24 Documents and PDFs

All roles · 8 steps

Step 1 of 8. This is the list of every printable document. Next, open the payment receipt. (#/doc/index)
Step 2 of 8. An official receipt with the fee breakdown and a dummy-payment line. Use Print or save as PDF in the top bar, then Next step. (#/doc/receipt/E-2026-0590)

Step 7 of 8. The full report template: cover, summary figures, tables with totals, method notes and page numbers. Download .csv saves the main table. (#/doc/report/credentials-issued)
Step 8 of 8. The ABC deposit batch, one row per ACR with totals. Download .csv saves the batch file. (#/doc/abc/ABC-FTMK-2026-03)
